key_insight: The paper fuses neural implicit representations with a factorized Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) latent model to learn parametric, high‑dimensional flows—separating parameter dependence from dynamics so the system can be predicted and interpolated efficiently.
problem_solved: How to model and predict temporal evolution of nonlinear, high‑dimensional physical systems across changing parameters without explicit governing equations or costly numerical solvers, enabling fast interpolation and real‑time use.
method: Use neural implicit networks to represent high‑dimensional states/fields continuously in space and time conditioned on parameters.
Factorize the latent representation into parameter and dynamical components and learn a DMD/linear evolution operator in the latent space to capture temporal behavior.
Train end‑to‑end to reconstruct states and to enable fast parameter interpolation and rollout via the learned latent dynamics (efficient reduced‑order prediction).
impact: Enables ML practitioners and engineers to build scalable, model‑free reduced‑order simulators for fast prediction, control, and parameter studies of complex physical systems without re-running expensive solvers.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: encoder/decoder with factorized latent (parameter vs dynamics) and a DMD-style linear operator acting in latent space.
Schematic showing parameter interpolation: how changing a parameter moves the parameter factor and yields different predicted flows.
Comparison charts: accuracy vs baseline and runtime/speedup (real‑time inference) for multiple parameter settings.
Latent mode visualization or eigenmode plot showing dominant dynamic modes learned by the DMD component.
paper_title: Factorized Neural Implicit DMD for Parametric Dynamics
paper_authors: Siyuan Chen, Zhecheng Wang, Yixin Chen, Yue Chang, Peter Yichen Chen
